messages:
Maya: heads-up — after the canary deploy (1732508000) i'm seeing a 200–400ms tail on chart paints in the console, mostly on pages with 3+ heatmaps :eyes:
Raj: got alerts from frontend-oncall about main-thread busy. what changed in the bundle in that rollout?
Maya: bundle overall size didn't spike, but the footer chunk now imports `i18n-polyfills` and starts `telemetry-sampler` synchronously on init. profiler shows long blocking task when many charts mount.
Oliver: deploy-bot shows the rollout was progressive (20%→50%→100% over ~45m). can we rollback the footer split quickly to confirm?
Deploy Bot: rollout 1732508000 (v2-footer-split) — prepared rollback to v2-footer-split@prev (manual action required) :warning:
Evelyn: before we full rollback, try this quick client patch: lazy-load the sampler and defer i18n polyfills until after first paint. example:
```
// pseudo
if (!window.Intl) import('i18n-polyfills')
requestIdleCallback(() => initTelemetrySampler())
```
Maya: tested locally — defers ~120ms of blocking, but charts still show ~150ms tail when 6+ series render concurrently. looks like prefetches are being aborted (429) then we fall back to sync `/api/metrics` calls that block render.
Raj: that smells like prefetch quota/routing mismatch. if prefetch requests hit the primary API and get rate-limited we end up doing sync fetches. can we get a network waterfall from a slow session?
Maya: pasted waterfall snippet:
GET /static/chunks/footer.8ab.js    200   12ms
GET /api/metrics?prefetch=true       429   35ms   (aborted)
GET /api/metrics?sync=true           200   160ms  (blocking)
Maya: note the aborted prefetchs — client retries synchronously which causes main-thread blocking when chart mounts wait for data.
Oliver: two fixes in parallel: 1) make prefetcher resilient (exponential backoff + concurrency cap) 2) routing policy change so prefetch=true prefers cache-tier.
Raj: +1. i'll add a routing rule: `route: prefer=cache-tier if header:prefetch=true` in the edge policy. EngInfra, can you pin the cache-tier so prefetches don't land on primary?
EngInfra: will coordinate. i can add a short-lived route override for the canary and watch metrics.
Frontend Oncall: muted duplicate alerts and extended the alert window to 5m to reduce noise during debug. will revert after verification.
Evelyn: plan: A) rollback footer split (fast), B) land prefetcher backoff + tests, C) add routing rule for prefetch header, D) run a 5% canary with synthetic chart load tests, then scale up. agreed?
Maya: yep. opening PR for the backoff + unit tests and attaching waterfall traces. :thumbsup:
Oliver: i'll queue the rollback now and schedule the 5% canary with the synthetic runner. if rollback doesn't clear stale client caches we may need to bump footer chunk hash to force reload.
Maya: doing rollback — will post status in ~6m.
